title: South Korea's direct cultural attendance fell in 2025 while active participation and cultural education rose
source_unit: South Korea Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism / Korea Culture and Tourism Institute, 2025 National Culture and Arts Activity Survey and National Leisure Activity Survey results
geography: South Korea; residents aged 15 and above across 17 metropolitan and provincial areas

observations.period: August 2024-July 2025 reference period; survey fielded August-November 2025

denominator.unit: South Korean residents aged 15 and above in the National Culture and Arts Activity Survey; 17 metropolitan and provincial areas

direct_cultural_event_attendance.unit: percent directly attending a cultural or arts event

popular_music_entertainment_attendance.unit: percent attending popular music or entertainment events

mechanism.value: The broad cultural-attendance rate is falling mainly through cinema, making aggregate participation sensitive to a high-reach commercial category rather than uniformly declining across all forms

observations.method: National Culture and Arts Activity Survey, an annual nationally approved statistic conducted through one-to-one household tablet interviews; the published reference period covers the prior year of cultural activity.
observations.uncertainty: The release reports self-reported attendance and year-over-year changes; it does not establish causes such as price, supply, screen substitution, household time, or venue closures.
observations.subgroup: Residents aged 15 and above across South Korea's 17 metropolitan and provincial areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: A cinema-led decline could coexist with stable or growing digital consumption, home-based culture, or other forms of participation not captured by the direct-attendance headline.

observations.period: August 2024-July 2025 reference period; active culture and arts engagement

denominator.unit: South Korean residents aged 15 and above in the National Culture and Arts Activity Survey

cultural_arts_event_participation.unit: percent participating directly in cultural or arts events, exhibitions, or creative activities

cultural_arts_education_experience.unit: percent with cultural or arts education experience

mechanism.value: Cultural engagement is becoming more active and learning-oriented even as passive or event-based attendance declines, suggesting a participation-mode transition rather than a simple cultural withdrawal

observations.method: The survey distinguishes direct viewing/attendance from participation in presentations, exhibitions, and creative activities, and separately measures cultural-arts education experience.
observations.uncertainty: The published shares do not identify whether active participation is a substitute for attendance, a complementary activity, or concentrated among already-engaged groups; no causal mechanism is estimated.
observations.subgroup: Residents aged 15 and above; national survey estimates across 17 metropolitan and provincial areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase may reflect survey wording, program availability, cohort composition, or low-base movement rather than a broad change in cultural identity or agency.

observations.period: August 2024-July 2025 reference period; leisure satisfaction and continuity

denominator.unit: South Korean residents aged 15 and above in the National Leisure Activity Survey; 17 metropolitan and provincial areas

leisure_satisfaction.unit: percent reporting satisfaction with leisure life

continuous_leisure_activity.unit: percent reporting continuous participation in leisure activities

mechanism.value: Leisure satisfaction and continuity can rise even while a major cultural-attendance measure falls, indicating that household leisure adaptation may preserve wellbeing through other activities, settings, or routines

observations.method: National Leisure Activity Survey conducted alongside the culture-and-arts survey; the release reports satisfaction and continuity measures for the prior reference year.
observations.uncertainty: Leisure is broader than culture and the release does not identify which activities generated satisfaction or continuity; these are descriptive associations, not welfare or causal estimates.
observations.subgroup: Residents aged 15 and above represented by the National Leisure Activity Survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher continuity may reflect routine low-cost or home-based activities rather than greater cultural opportunity, and satisfaction is subjective and context-dependent.

related_sources.claim: Official Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism release reporting the 2025 culture, arts, leisure, and worker-leave survey results.
Official survey notice documents the nationally approved surveys, 15+ target population, household interview method, and 2025 fieldwork period.

boundary: This record adds South Korean evidence on cultural attendance, active participation, cultural education, and broader leisure continuity. The sources are official self-report surveys and do not establish causal reasons for the attendance decline, actual spending, digital substitution, or equal cultural access.
